objective.statement: Recognise the breve and the breve rest, and use them in 4/2.
successCriteria: I know a breve lasts as long as two semibreves.
I know a breve fills a whole bar of 4/2.
I can write the breve rest for a silent bar of 4/2.

explanation.text: You already know the semibreve, the longest note in most music. A breve is longer still: it lasts as long as two semibreves, which is four minims or eight crotchets. It is sometimes called the double whole note. It is written as a semibreve-shaped head with a vertical line on each side, or as a small box.

music.textAlternative: One bar of 4/2 holding a single breve.

explanation.caption: A breve fills one whole bar of 4/2.

explanation.text: Remember what 4/2 means: four minim beats in every bar. Four minims make two semibreves, and two semibreves make exactly one breve. So a single breve fills a bar of 4/2 on its own.

Every note has a rest of the same length, and the breve is no exception. The breve rest is a solid block that fills the whole space between the third and fourth lines of the stave. It is used for a silent bar of 4/2.

music.textAlternative: One bar of 4/2 holding a single breve rest.

explanation.caption: The breve rest: a silent bar of 4/2.

explanation.text: 4/2 is the one time signature in which a silent bar is a breve rest. In every other time signature a silent bar is a semibreve rest.

steps: Hold one note for all four: that is the breve.
It lasts as long as two semibreves tied together.
demonstration.textAlternative: A single breve fills a bar of 4/2: four minim beats.

guided.prompt: How many minims last as long as one breve?

2.reason: That is half the number. A breve is twice as long as a semibreve, so you need twice as many of the shorter notes as you would for a semibreve.

8.reason: That is double. A semibreve is the one that lasts as long as that many; a breve is twice a semibreve, not four times.

A breve is two semibreves. A semibreve is two minims, a minim two crotchets.

feedback.correct: Yes: a breve is twice a semibreve.

mistakes.halved-or-doubled: Each step down the note values halves the length; each step up doubles it.
mistakes.dot-misread: Each dot adds half of the value before it.
mistakes.note-rest-confusion: Check the shape carefully. A rest that hangs below its line lasts longer than one that sits on top of it.
mistakes.tie-dot-confusion: A tie adds separate notes together; a dot adds half the note's own value.
mistakes.tuplet-ignored: Those notes are a tuplet, so they share a different amount of time. Look at the number written over them.

feedback.fallback: Not quite. Try counting each value in crotchet beats.

provenance.notes: Original wording. Follows Grade 4 outcome 2 and First Steps Grade 4 section 1 (p. 79, read in the PDF): breve = two semibreves, fills 4/2, the breve rest fills the space between the third and fourth lines, 4/2 is the only time signature whose silent bar is not a semibreve rest. The book's second form of the breve sign (a box) is described in words because the notation renderer draws only one form.
